text:
The man is likely to prevail. When the woman conveyed her house to him, he owned both the dominant and servient parcels, and the easement was extinguished by merger. His later warranty deed didn't create a new easement, and the recording doesn't revive one. No implied easement arose either, because he never used the path while he owned both lots. The team note's claim that a recorded appurtenant easement survives common-ownership merger is wrong under the common-law rule, so I'm not adopting it.

CONFIDENCE: 82
